question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Velocity of a Particle at the Moment When Its Acceleration is Zero
question.problem:
A particle $P$ is traveling along the $x$-axis with displacement $s(t)$ from a fixed origin $O$ given by

$$
s(t)=2{t}^{3}-9{t}^{2}+3t-2,\,t\ge 0.
$$

Find the time at which the acceleration is zero, and find the value of the velocity at this moment.
question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}-9{t}^{2}+3t-2) \\  & =6{t}^{2}-18t+3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{2}-18t+3) \\  & =12t-18\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we put $a=0$ to find the time when the acceleration is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}12t-18 & =0 \\ t & =\frac{18}{12} \\ t & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the acceleration is zero when $t=\frac{3}{2}.$ To find the velocity at this moment, we substitute this back into $v(t)$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{3}{2}) & =6{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2}-18(\frac{3}{2})+3 \\  & =6(\frac{9}{4})-27+3 \\  & =\frac{27}{2}-27+3 \\  & =-\frac{21}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
